messages:
ravi: Heads up — seeing a spike in 502/504s from the internal L4 LB to gpu-serving in us-west-2a rack rc1. Only affects RDMA-enabled pods. Latency tail and retransmits high.

kyra: Noted. Is it across all zones or just rc1?

ravi: Just rc1 so far. rc2/rc3 look fine. Affected jobs are both inference and some training checkpoints that use GPUDirect/RDMA.

sasha: Any recent infra changes? ToR config, MTU, EVPN, or BGP timers?

ravi: We pushed a ToR ACL tweak last night and bumped MTU on hosts to 9000 last week. I wonder if there's an MTU mismatch.

max: Can we get a quick packet sample? If RDMA path MTU mismatches you'll see drops on the switch side and retransmits on TCP.

ravi: Pasted quick dumps: ````
# ip -s link show bond0
3: bond0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 1234567890 packets 1234567 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 987654321 packets 987654 errors 120 dropped 0 overruns 0 carrier 0
````

ravi: And tcpdump from a healthy pod -> LB: ````
12:01:02.123456 IP pod-abc > lb-svc: Flags [P.], seq 1001:2000, ack 5001, win 65535
12:01:02.223789 IP pod-abc > lb-svc: Flags [P.], seq 2001:3000, ack 5001, win 65535 (retransmission)
````

net-bot: ALERT: link flaps detected on spine-rc1-2 at 2026-03-17T23:55:14Z — BFD session restarted 4x in 5m.

kyra: OK bfd flaps + MTU differences smell bad. Which vendor on the leafs?

ravi: leafs are Mellanox Spectrum-based with Arista/EVPN fabric on spines. ToR model is Arista 7150.

max: Mellanox RDMA drivers require consistent MTU across end-to-end path. If ToR/LEAFs are set to 1500 while hosts expect 9000, RDMA connection establishment can fail silently and fall back or drop. That matches RDMA job failures.

sasha: Also seeing weird asymmetric flows in L4 stats — front-end LB hashes are ECMPing to a different ToR than the return path. Could be hash key mismatch after the ACL change.

ravi: I ran iperf between affected host pair across rc1: ````
# iperf3 -c 10.1.20.45 -P 8
Connecting to host 10.1.20.45, port 5201
[  5] local 10.1.20.11 port 52034 connected to 10.1.20.45 port 5201
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  9.35 GBytes  8.02 Gbits/sec  (sender)
[  6]   0.00-10.00  sec  1.12 GBytes  963 Mbits/sec  (receiver)
````

ravi: Sender shows full, receiver much lower -> indicates asymmetric path or drops.

kyra: Can you check ethtool counters on the ToR-facing host interfaces and ToR counters for CRC/fragmented packets?

ravi: ethtool on host shows tx_errors on host NIC. I pulled ToR logs: several "fragmentation needed" and "MTU mismatch" warnings around the time jobs start.

max: Two-pronged mitigation: 1) temporarily set host MTU back to 1500 for RDMA workloads (quick but causes performance loss), or 2) fix fabric by aligning ToR and spine MTU to 9000 and remediate BFD flaps. Which is faster?

oncall: I'll coordinate with network team. Rolling change window in 15m for ToR MTU alignment across rc1 leafs and spine 2. If that fails, we'll fallback hosts to 1500 on affected nodes.

sasha: Before we change MTU, can we also disable the ACL tweak from last night on the impacted ToR? That was the only config we changed recently.

net-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: rolled back ACL on fanout-rc1-03 at 23:12:01Z by infra-ops.

ravi: After ACL rollback + ToR MTU align, I see LB metrics recovering: retransmits dropping and 5xxs down to baseline. RDMA jobs resuming checkpoints.

kyra: Nice. Can we add a health-check to LB that detects RDMA handshake failures (or MTU mismatches)? We should auto-alert earlier.

max: Filing infra issue to add MTU consistency probe and a BFD flap alert threshold: INFRA-1254. Also add a runbook entry for host MTU rollback path.

oncall: TL;DR: root cause = config drift (ACL tweak) + intermittent BFD flaps exposing an MTU mismatch on rc1 path -> asymmetric ECMP and packet fragmentation for RDMA -> internal LB 5xxs. Rollback + MTU alignment fixed it.

ravi: Confirmed healthy at 23:47 UTC. Leaving the thread open for postmortem writeup. :thumbsup:
